decisions.reason: The existing message-842 MODIFY already captures the battery, USB-C, and display-connector layout constraints, so no additional or corrected Event is needed.
This Requirement concerns superseded interboard alignment rules; the new integrated-board edge-placement constraints do not alter its current legacy-status state.
The antenna clause is already captured by the candidate's message-842 MODIFY with the required orientation and 3 mm keepout.
Connector edge placement does not change the established single-board architecture or board count.
The source specifies connector placement on the integrated board and does not reinstate or change the superseded standalone main-board form factor.
The connector-layout constraints do not establish or modify any PCB layer-count requirement.
The source imposes physical placement constraints but does not change the cost objective, component-selection policy, integrated architecture, or interboard-connector strategy.
The referenced display connectors are J_DISP_SPI, J_DISP_I2C, and J_DISP_LED, not the J_LED_CHG charge-status interface; its behavior and electrical definition remain unchanged.
Placing J_BAT on a short edge does not change the NTC terminal, thermal-protection function, or controller requirements.
The physical locations of J_BAT and USB-C do not alter DCDC1 voltage regulation, current rating, powered loads, or Schottky-drop compensation.
The USB-C edge constraint affects physical connector layout, while this Requirement's enumeration, flashing, data-line, sourcing, and programming-port semantics remain unchanged.

The J_BAT location constraint does not resolve or modify the connector family, pitch, pin count, pin functions, part number, or unresolved pin order; physical placement is already owned by the connector-layout Requirements.
